title: Path independence of inertia invariants
statement: Let $C_0/k_0$ be a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup], let $j:U_0\hookrightarrow C_0$ be a nonempty open with finite complement $S_0$, and let $s\in S_0$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse Weil $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-sheaf on $U_0$, choose a geometric base point $\bar u$ on $U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\rho:W(U_0,\bar u)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$, where $V=\mathcal F_{\bar u}$, be its Weil fundamental representation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. Let $D_s$, $I_s$, $W(K_s)$ and the path-dependent decomposition homomorphisms $\theta_1,\theta_2$ be as in [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing], obtained from two choices of path from the same local geometric point to $\bar u$. For $a=1,2$, let $V_{s,a}$ be the space $V$ equipped with the $W(K_s)$-action $\rho\circ\theta_a|_{W(K_s)}$, and define $V_{s,a}^{I_s}=\{v\in V:\rho(\theta_a(i))v=v\text{ for every }i\in I_s\}$. These are equivalently the invariants under the subgroup $\theta_a(I_s)\subset W(U_0,\bar u)$ of [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. For a residue geometric Frobenius lift $\Phi\in W(K_s)$, let $T_a$ be the restriction of $\rho(\theta_a(\Phi))$ to $V_{s,a}^{I_s}$; this is a well-defined automorphism independent of the lift by [lem-real-boundary-frobenius-invariants], applied to the normal subgroup $I_s$ of $W(K_s)$. Then there is a linear isomorphism $A:V_{s,1}^{I_s}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{s,2}^{I_s}$ with $A T_1=T_2 A$.

proof.text: Write $\gamma_1,\gamma_2:F_{\bar\eta_s}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar u}$ for the two paths [def-real-boundary-decomposition-path]. The composite $g=\gamma_2\gamma_1^{-1}$ is a natural automorphism of $F_{\bar u}$, hence an element of $\pi_1(U_0,\bar u)$ by [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Substitution in $\theta_a(\sigma)=\gamma_a a_\sigma\gamma_a^{-1}$ from [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing] gives $\theta_2(\sigma)=g\theta_1(\sigma)g^{-1}$ for every $\sigma\in D_s$.

Use the arithmetic projection $p$ and the compatible identification $G_s=\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_s)$ of [lem-real-boundary-local-constants]. The residue extension $k_s/k_0$ is finite by that lemma. Put $h=p(g)$ and let $F\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ be geometric Frobenius. By [det-base-field-cd-galois-group], $k_s/k_0$ is finite Galois and its automorphism group is generated by arithmetic Frobenius, hence also by its inverse $F|_{k_s}$. Choose $n\in\mathbf Z$ with $h|_{k_s}=F^n|_{k_s}$. The element $F^{-n}h$ fixes $k_s$; the image assertion of [lem-real-boundary-local-constants] gives $\delta\in D_s$ with $p(\theta_1(\delta))=F^{-n}h$. Put $d=\theta_1(\delta)$ and $w=gd^{-1}$. Then $p(w)=h(F^{-n}h)^{-1}=F^n$, so $w\in W(U_0,\bar u)$ by [def-wf-weil-group] and $g=wd$. This is the source's degree argument written on the finite quotient $\operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k_0)$; it does not require evaluating $\rho$ at $g$ or $d$.

Since $I_s=\ker r_s$, conjugation by $\delta$ and $\delta^{-1}$ preserves $I_s$. Thus $\theta_2(i)=w\theta_1(\delta i\delta^{-1})w^{-1}$ for $i\in I_s$, by Step 1 and $g=w\theta_1(\delta)$. As $i$ ranges over $I_s$, so does $\delta i\delta^{-1}$. Consequently $\theta_2(I_s)=w\theta_1(I_s)w^{-1}$. The subgroup landing assertion of [lem-real-boundary-decomposition-landing] ensures that all the inertia images in this equality lie in $W(U_0,\bar u)$, where $\rho$ is defined.

For $v\in V_{s,1}^{I_s}$ and $i\in I_s$, the formula of Step 3 gives $\rho(\theta_2(i))\rho(w)v=\rho(w)\rho(\theta_1(\delta i\delta^{-1}))v=\rho(w)v$. Hence $\rho(w)$ maps the first invariant space into the second. Conversely, if $v_2$ is fixed by $\theta_2(I_s)$, the same equality of subgroups shows that $\rho(w^{-1})v_2$ is fixed by $\theta_1(I_s)$. The restrictions of $\rho(w)$ and $\rho(w^{-1})$ are inverse linear maps. Define $A$ to be this restriction of $\rho(w)$, using the linear representation and invariant-space conventions of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] and [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. In the current definition, $W$ is the fibre product with $\mathbf Z$ and $\rho(hs^n)=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(h)T_s^n$ is explicitly a continuous representation on that entire group. We use its group-homomorphism law and linear inverses; no action of the full arithmetic fundamental group on $V$ is assumed.

source.place: last sentence, identification of invariant spaces

proof.text: The residue group $G_s$ is abelian by [det-base-field-cd-galois-group]. Therefore $r_s(\delta\Phi\delta^{-1})=r_s(\Phi)$, so $\delta\Phi\delta^{-1}\in W(K_s)$ and it lies in the same coset of $I_s$ as $\Phi$. Apply [lem-real-boundary-frobenius-invariants] to $G=W(K_s)$, $N=I_s$ and $\alpha=\rho\circ\theta_1|_{W(K_s)}$: on $V_{s,1}^{I_s}$, $\rho(\theta_1(\delta\Phi\delta^{-1}))$ equals $T_1$. By Step 1, $\theta_2(\Phi)=w\theta_1(\delta\Phi\delta^{-1})w^{-1}$. Thus for every $v\in V_{s,1}^{I_s}$ one has $T_2Av=\rho(\theta_2(\Phi))\rho(w)v=\rho(w)\rho(\theta_1(\delta\Phi\delta^{-1}))v=AT_1v$. The same quotient-action lemma supplies the lift-independent automorphisms $T_a$ in the statement. This proves the required Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism.
